stories.title: Marina Shafir cuts post-Collision promo on Mercedes Moné
stories.tldr: Following the recent episode of AEW Collision, Death Riders member Marina Shafir delivered a pointed backstage promo directed at AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Mone. Shafir expressed her respect for Mone while highlighting their stylistic differences, noting that she relies on her in-ring work rather than elaborate entrances or production. This challenge follows Shafir's recent confrontation with Mone on Dynamite and a busy night on Collision that included a mixed tag team victory and a post-show brawl.

stories.title: Bryan & Vinny recap WWE SmackDown and AEW Collision
stories.tldr: The latest episode of The Bryan & Vinny Show features comprehensive reviews of both WWE SmackDown and AEW Collision. The hosts break down two contrasting wrestling programs, describing AEW Collision as having way too much going on while WWE SmackDown featured far too little content. Despite the opposite pacing issues of the two shows, the hosts provide an entertaining and detailed discussion covering all the action.

stories.title: AEW news round-up covering Kairi Sane negotiations and New Year's Smash
stories.tldr: AEW remains in ongoing discussions with former WWE Women's Champion Kairi Sane, though she is also weighing competing offers from promotions in Japan. In addition to contract negotiations, the company has locked down New Level to five-year agreements running through the summer of 2031. On the live event side, AEW officially announced a two-night New Year's Smash event in Atlanta for January 1 and 2, a major attraction that has been on the schedule for months. Furthermore, recent independent bookings for The Dogs allowed the group to creatively incorporate their on-screen AEW storyline split into a PRODUCE Wrestling event.

stories.title: Jonathan Gresham comments on potential return to ROH under Tony Khan
stories.tldr: Former ROH World Champion Jonathan Gresham recently discussed his 2022 falling out with AEW President Tony Khan, which occurred after Gresham was abruptly told to drop his title at Death Before Dishonor. Although Gresham subsequently requested and received his release, his multiple attempts to reach out and apologize to Khan have been rebuffed. Despite the current cold shoulder, Gresham remains open to eventually settling their differences and potentially returning to Ring of Honor. Meanwhile, he is heavily focused on recovering from serious health issues, coaching, scouting, and launching his own upcoming wrestling promotion.

stories.title: Paige (Saraya) stranded in Scotland following flight cancelations
stories.tldr: Former WWE Superstar Paige experienced a severe travel nightmare while trying to leave Scotland due to a combination of overbooking and severe weather. After her morning flight was canceled because her ticket was inexplicably given away and a storm struck the area, her backup plan of taking a seven-hour train to London also failed. She is now stranded and hoping to successfully make her journey home tomorrow.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett defends making his CMLL debut
stories.tldr: AEW star and WWE Hall of Famer Jeff Jarrett recently addressed the online backlash he received regarding his debut appearance at the CMLL 93rd Aniversario event where he faced Blue Panther. Despite the mixed reactions from internet fans, Jarrett defended his selective in-ring appearances and pointed out that the live crowd inside Arena Mexico was fully engaged with his match. The 40-year veteran also discussed his current role in professional wrestling, emphasizing that he carefully picks his spots to help elevate younger talent rather than competing as a weekly main eventer.

stories.title: Anthony Bowens reflects on joining AEW and forming The Acclaimed
stories.tldr: Anthony Bowens recently reflected on his journey to All Elite Wrestling, where he signed in October 2020 after previously considering an offer from WWE. Tony Khan paired Bowens with Max Caster to form The Acclaimed, a move that led to multiple championship reigns despite the two wrestlers barely knowing each other beforehand. Now, years later, both Bowens and Caster have become free agents, with Caster currently stepping away from the ring to attend therapy.

stories.title: Rebel receives hometown honor in Owasso, Oklahoma
stories.tldr: Former All Elite Wrestling personality Rebel, also known as Tanea Brooks, was recently inducted into the Owasso High School Hall of Fame in her hometown of Oklahoma. She shared her gratitude on social media, expressing how much the hometown recognition meant to her and thanking those who made the event possible. This special honor follows her recent appointment as an honorary member of the I Am ALS Board of Directors earlier this month.

stories.title: Garrett Borden pays homage to father Sting ahead of AEW Collision
stories.tldr: Garrett Borden, son of wrestling legend Sting, competed in a dark match ahead of the October 24 episode of AEW Collision, defeating Kiran Grey with a TKO finisher and paying tribute to his father with multiple Stinger Splashes. The match took place in the same historic building where Sting made his iconic Fall Brawl 1996 appearance, adding extra significance to the evening. Borden is currently training at the Rhodes Wrestling Academy and prepares to team up with his brother Steven Borden for the first time in November, following Steven's return from an injury suffered at AEW All Out.

stories.title: Samoa Joe names his hardest-hitting opponent
stories.tldr: During a recent interview with SHAK Wrestling, AEW star Samoa Joe participated in a bracket-style game to determine the hardest-hitting opponent of his storied career. Facing a gauntlet of legendary names from ROH, TNA, WWE, and AEW, Joe ultimately narrowed the field down to Brock Lesnar and Kenta Kobashi. Weighing factors like raw power, technique, and destructive potential, Joe officially crowned Brock Lesnar as the hardest-hitting opponent he has ever faced in the ring.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett wishes he had a rematch with specific WWE Hall of Famer
stories.tldr: AEW star Jeff Jarrett recently revealed during his podcast that one of his biggest career regrets is never getting a singles rematch against Shawn Michaels. The two wrestling veterans previously faced off for the Intercontinental Championship at a WWF event in July 1995. Jarrett humorously admitted that his own abrupt departure from the company immediately after the match ruined any possibility of running the program back.

stories.title: Elayna Black (Brianna Coda) AEW history and move speculation
stories.tldr: Before signing with WWE and eventually TNA Wrestling, Brianna Coda competed as Elayna Black on AEW Dark back in 2020. Recent speculation questioned whether she might return to AEW following her WWE departure. While she expressed interest last year, reports indicate no concrete talks occurred before she joined TNA. Furthermore, backstage sources confirmed that skipping an earlier AEW extra work opportunity to attend a WWE tryout created no negative issues within the company.

stories.title: Jay White's new AEW faction undergoes rapid name changes
stories.tldr: Jay White's newly formed faction has already undergone a rapid name change just hours after its debut. Following heavy fan criticism of their original moniker on social media, White released a post-show promo revealing the group's new name. AEW has already updated its official roster page to reflect the adjustment.

stories.title: AEW Full Gear 2026 card updates and match additions
stories.tldr: The AEW Full Gear card continues to expand with several new championship matches announced for the November event. Swerve Strickland has secured a rematch for the AEW World Trios Championship alongside New Level, though Hangman Page has currently declined the Texas Death stipulation Strickland wanted. Additional title bouts added to the card feature the Young Bucks defending their tag team titles and the Brawling Birds defending the women's tag team championships.

stories.title: MJF makes surprise indie wrestling return amid AEW hiatus
stories.tldr: MJF broke his AEW television hiatus by appearing at the Create A Pro Wrestling Academy on October 25 to serve as a special guest referee. During the event, he entertained the crowd with his signature antics before officiating a 12-man tag team match. Although he has been absent since All In on August 30, MJF recently teased that his time away is part of a deliberate plan. When he eventually returns to television, he intends to immediately target the world championship and become the company's first undisputed champion.

stories.title: Tommaso Ciampa promos on AEW's Andrade El Idolo following Collision
stories.tldr: Following his WrestleDream defeat to AEW National Champion Andrade El Idolo, WWE star Tommaso Ciampa is escalating their feud. Ciampa recently attacked Andrade and Mike Bailey on AEW Collision after a tag team match. In a fiery backstage promo, Ciampa admitted he previously underestimated Andrade and vowed to come for blood and the championship in their next encounter.

stories.title: Anthony Bowens sparks NJPW speculation after AEW contract expiration
stories.tldr: Former AEW star Anthony Bowens has fueled speculation about a potential move to New Japan Pro Wrestling after sharing a photo outside the NJPW LA Dojo on social media. His contract with All Elite Wrestling is believed to have expired on October 1, following his final appearance at the AEW All In London Buy-In pre-show. Although Bowens recently hinted in an interview that he has a preferred direction for the next chapter of his career, no official confirmation has been made regarding contract negotiations or his future destination.

stories.title: AEW Women's Blood & Guts match teams announced
stories.tldr: The official lineups for the women and men's Blood and Guts matches have been announced for the upcoming November 4 special edition of Dynamite in Jacksonville. The women's match will feature Willow Nightingale, Wrathlander, and the Brawling Birds battling Divine Dominion and the Triangle of Madness following weeks of backstage ambushes and ring interferences. Meanwhile, the men's match pits Will Ospreay, Adam Copeland, Steven Borden, The Young Bucks, and Darby Allin against the Don Callis Family. Fans can watch the special event live on TBS and HBO Max.

stories.title: TNT Championship match added to AEW Fright Night Dynamite
stories.tldr: Josh Alexander challenged Darby Allin to a TNT Championship match for the upcoming Fright Night Dynamite after picking up a dominant victory on Collision. Alexander stated his desire to bring gold to the Don Callis Family and also targeted Adam Copeland for a future title defense. The segment led to a chaotic brawl involving Copeland, the Don Callis Family, and multiple other wrestlers who are also set for the upcoming Blood and Guts match. AEW officially confirmed the title match for the October 28 special episode in St. Louis, Missouri.

stories.title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 PPV buys trending near low numbers
stories.tldr: AEW WrestleDream 2026 is currently projected to finish with between 100,000 and 110,000 pay-per-view buys, matching the company's lowest figures of the year set by AEW Redemption. While domestic purchases have experienced a decline, international growth has shown positive momentum, particularly driven by platforms like HBO Max. The event was headlined by Will Ospreay successfully defending the AEW World Championship in an eight-man Clockwork Carnage match in front of 7,173 fans. Industry reports suggest that the company's recent scheduling shift to Saturday nights and the international appeal of stars like Ospreay may be driving these shifting geographic buyrate trends.

stories.title: Artist Of Stardom Championship match set for AEW Fright Night Collision
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling has announced that an Artist of Stardom Championship match will be taped for an upcoming Fright Night Collision episode in St. Louis. The reigning champions, Triangle of Madness, will defend their belts against the STARDOM trio of Hazuki, Koguma, and Fuwa-chan. This high-stakes encounter stems from a heated brawl that broke out following a title defense in September at Stardom To The World.

stories.title: Kamille absence noted during AEW birthday post
stories.tldr: AEW recently posted a birthday message for Kamille on social media, which inadvertently sparked widespread fan questioning regarding her prolonged absence from television. While reports confirm she remains under contract with the company, she has barely appeared on programming following a brief feud-ending loss to Willow Nightingale earlier this year. Fans and insiders alike have noted a lack of long-term creative plans for the former NWA Women's Champion since her initial removal from storylines involving Mercedes Mone.

stories.title: AEW Fright Night Dynamite ticket sales update
stories.tldr: AEW Fright Night Dynamite is set to emanate from the Chaifetz Arena in Saint Louis this upcoming Wednesday with nearly 2,800 tickets distributed so far. Ticket sales have seen a recent bump, adding over 430 distributed seats in just a five-day span. The special themed broadcast features a high-profile match card highlighted by a championship bout and a high-stakes tag team series match.

stories.title: Samoa Joe comments on retirement mindset
stories.tldr: AEW star Samoa Joe recently discussed his current career mindset and retirement perspective during an interview with SHAK Wrestling following a filming hiatus. Joe stated that his main goal is to deliver meaningful and entertaining matches for fans while building lasting memories before his eventual retirement, though he has not finalized a specific timeline. He also expressed a desire to give back to the wrestling industry and enrich the communities that supported him throughout his travels, hoping to leave the business in a much better place.

stories.title: Tommaso Ciampa praises Andrade's work in AEW
stories.tldr: WWE star Tommaso Ciampa recently praised Andrade El Idolo, stating that the AEW National Champion is currently performing at the highest level of his career. Despite their ongoing rivalry and recent match at AEW WrestleDream where Andrade retained his title, Ciampa highlighted Andrade's incredible fan reactions and their parallel career paths. The two wrestlers previously crossed paths in WWE before reigniting their rivalry in AEW.

stories.title: Jay White reveals new name for AEW faction 'The Last Outfit'
stories.tldr: Jay White officially named his newly merged faction with The Dogs The Last Outfit on Collision after briefly teasing a Bullet Club revival. Setting his sights on Jon Moxley and the Continental Championship, White went on to defeat Kyle O'Reilly in the main event. The night ended in chaotic brawling when Orange Cassidy accidentally struck Moxley, allowing White to capitalize with another Blade Runner.

stories.title: MVP denies reports that Hurt Syndicate refused to put over talent in AEW
stories.tldr: MVP has strongly pushed back against recent internet rumors claiming that The Hurt Syndicate refused to put other talent over in AEW. In a series of social media posts, he labeled the reports as blatant lies and insisted the group actually wanted to work with younger wrestlers. He specifically noted that they wanted to drop their tag team titles back to Private Party. MVP also dismissed claims of a cancelled Bobby Lashley and Swerve Strickland rematch and hinted that a deliberate whisper campaign is behind the negative press.

stories.title: Ilja Dragunov reflects on decision to join AEW and his new theme music
stories.tldr: Following his move to AEW, Ilja Dragunov has revealed that lingering doubts after returning from an ACL tear and dropping the United States title led him to decline WWE's contract renewal for a fresh start. He also detailed the emotional significance of bringing back his independent circuit entrance music, Soviet March, to match his artsy persona. Fresh off that memorable debut, Dragunov quickly transitioned to the ring by defeating Speedball Mike Bailey on Dynamite.

stories.title: Former WWE announcer Samantha Irvin approaching free agency; not expected in AEW immediately
stories.tldr: Samantha Irvin is nearing the end of her WWE non-compete period this month, sparking speculation about her wrestling future. While AEW has internally discussed bringing her in for an on-screen role, she is not expected to debut immediately. Irvin, who is married to AEW star Ricochet, has previously expressed interest in managing and potentially working alongside her husband.

stories.title: Billy Gunn reflects on his AEW in-ring work and pairing with The Acclaimed
stories.tldr: Billy Gunn recently discussed his unexpected in-ring resurgence in AEW alongside The Acclaimed. Initially signed to a limited 12-date contract primarily for backstage coaching, Gunn ended up performing regularly on television well into his sixties. He credited his lifelong dedication to fitness for allowing him to keep up with much younger talent.

stories.title: Details emerge on health history of former AEW star PAC
stories.tldr: Following the sudden passing of former AEW star PAC due to bronchial asthma, new details have emerged regarding his prior health history. Reports indicate the wrestler had previously dealt with lung-related issues and blood clots, which carefully dictated his international travel schedule. Medical experts have since weighed in on the rare nature of fatal asthma attacks and how past pulmonary issues could theoretically impact complication risks.

stories.title: Samantha Irvin's WWE non-compete expiring and potential AEW interest
stories.tldr: Former WWE ring announcer Samantha Irvin, who now goes by her real name Samantha Johnson, is set to become a free agent as her strict two-year non-compete agreement expires. Johnson left WWE in October 2024 under an unusual unpaid arrangement after quitting before her three-year contract concluded. While All Elite Wrestling has internally discussed bringing her in for an on-screen role, an immediate debut is not currently planned. As she focuses on her music career and explores her future, a potential arrival in AEW alongside her husband Ricochet remains a possibility further down the road.

stories.title: AEW's Willow Nightingale provides injury update on broken hand
stories.tldr: Former AEW Women's World Champion Willow Nightingale has provided a new update on her ongoing recovery from a broken hand sustained this summer. During an Instagram Q&A, she revealed that while the hand is improving, it is not yet one hundred percent healed and still requires daily use of a bone stimulator. Despite battling the injury through major events like AEW All In and All Out, Nightingale has continued to remain active on television as part of ongoing storylines with her stablemates.

stories.title: Sheamus free agency rumors and AEW interest
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Sheamus became a free agent after rejecting a contract extension earlier this year, sparking widespread speculation about his wrestling future. Although top AEW talent like Claudio Castagnoli and Adam Copeland reportedly support him joining the promotion, management does not appear to be in an immediate rush to sign him. Meanwhile, Sheamus has been sharing intense gym workouts online and has booked a convention appearance on the same day as an upcoming AEW pay-per-view, keeping fans guessing about his next move.

stories.title: Tony Schiavone discusses AEW commentary, production, and working on the fly
stories.tldr: AEW commentator Tony Schiavone recently discussed the company's behind-the-scenes production process on his podcast, revealing that the broadcast team and roster frequently handle last-minute changes and minimal preparation. Speaking with guests Clark Connors and David Finlay, Schiavone noted that the commentary team often learns about script adjustments at the exact same time as the wrestlers and fans. Despite these spontaneous shifts, Schiavone and Connors praised the production staff and talent for their ability to work on the fly and consistently deliver a polished, high-quality show.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite viewership ratings for October 21
stories.tldr: The October 21 episode of AEW Dynamite drew an average of 661,000 viewers on TBS alongside a 0.15 rating in the key 18 to 49 demographic. While total linear cable viewership saw a slight drop compared to the previous week's specific Dynamite portion, the key demo rating actually experienced an increase. The broadcast also achieved significant year-over-year growth when compared to the same week in October 2025. Additionally, the show featured major moments like Steven Borden's return and Ilja Dragunov's debut match that drove strong digital engagement.

stories.title: Reason for AEW stars missing October 21 Dynamite
stories.tldr: Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed missed the October 21 episode of AEW Dynamite to attend the wedding of their longtime friend and former WWE stablemate, Big E, who married Kris Yim. According to Dave Meltzer, their absence was entirely unrelated to creative plans or their ongoing storyline as part of The New Level. With Kingston and Creed away, their stablemate Swerve Strickland carried the group's storyline forward by appearing alone in a backstage segment to challenge AEW World Trios Champions Hangman Adam Page and Brodido to a rematch at Full Gear.

stories.title: AEW Blood & Guts ticket distribution updates
stories.tldr: Ticket sales for the upcoming AEW Dynamite Blood and Guts episode have experienced a notable surge, with over 1,000 tickets distributed in the span of a single week to bring the total to an estimated 3,068. The high-profile event is scheduled for Wednesday, November 4, at the VyStar Veterans Memorial Arena in Jacksonville, Florida. Fans are securing their seats ahead of the broadcast on TBS and HBO Max, which features a massive 12-man tag team match inside the signature double-ring steel structure.

stories.title: AEW announces two-night New Year's Smash 2027 special
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling has officially announced a two-night New Year's Smash 2027 special taking place on Friday, January 1, and Saturday, January 2, 2027. The event emanates live from the Gateway Center Arena in Atlanta, Georgia, featuring Dynamite moving to a special Friday night time slot followed by Saturday's Collision. Tickets will go on general public sale on October 30, with early access and presales beginning in late October. Talent such as Mercedes Mone, Persephone, The New Level, and Kevin Knight are currently featured on the promotional advertising for the Atlanta event.

stories.title: Tony Schiavone reveals backstage concerns over AEW Clockwork Carnage match
stories.tldr: AEW commentator Tony Schiavone recently admitted on his podcast that backstage personnel had serious doubts about the experimental Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream 2026. Despite extensive meetings and briefings explaining the eight-person elimination and points-based format, everyone in the back remained uncertain how the concept would actually translate on pay-per-view. However, Schiavone was ultimately won over by the high-stakes drama in the closing stretch as Will Ospreay successfully defended the AEW World Championship.

stories.title: Tony Khan discusses Adam Copeland and Christian Cage in AEW
stories.tldr: AEW CEO Tony Khan recently discussed major updates regarding Adam Copeland and Christian Cage during a media call following Copeland's announcement that he plans to retire from in-ring competition in 2027. Khan confirmed he was aware of Copeland's upcoming retirement timeline and praised the legendary wrestler's storied career ahead of his final run. Additionally, Khan addressed the severe injuries Christian Cage sustained during their AEW Tag Team Championship Ladder Match at All Out, which left Cage with multiple broken ribs and a collapsed lung. While Cage is currently recovering with an uncertain return timeline, Copeland continues his singles pursuits in AEW, recently coming up short in a world championship match at WrestleDream.

stories.title: Austin Creed on adapting to AEW's tag team style
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Austin Creed is confident that he and his long-time tag team partner Kofi can seamlessly adapt to AEW's distinct style following their recent move. Drawing on their vast experience, including Creed's past tenure in TNA Wrestling, the duo views themselves as adaptable chameleons and versatile Swiss Army knives capable of handling any role. Already finding success by capturing the AEW Trios Championship before dropping it at WrestleDream, the pair is also enjoying the additional non-wrestling opportunities provided by their new contracts.

stories.title: Conrad Thompson addresses Roman Reigns criticism
stories.tldr: Podcast host Conrad Thompson recently addressed accusations from WWE champion Roman Reigns that Thompson criticized him just to chase views or due to alleged ties with AEW. Thompson defended his stance, maintaining that he simply shared his honest wrestling opinion and has no corporate allegiance to any promotion. He pointed to his personal friendships within WWE, including Charlotte Flair and Cody Rhodes, while expressing surprise at the massive backlash his comments generated.

stories.title: AEW's Taya Valkyrie launches music career with debut EP
stories.tldr: AEW star Taya Valkyrie has officially entered the music industry by releasing her debut four-track EP titled Fake. Dropping on Friday, October 23, the project includes the tracks Witch, Treat, Fight, and the title song. Valkyrie celebrated the launch on social media as part of her birthday celebration, urging fans to stream and add the songs to their playlists. The new EP is currently available across major streaming platforms such as Spotify, Apple Music, and YouTube, marking an exciting new creative venture outside of professional wrestling.

stories.title: Jay White segment and match added to AEW Collision
stories.tldr: Jay White is scheduled to address the fans on Saturday's AEW Collision following a shocking betrayal on Dynamite involving the Bang Bang Gang and The Dogs. Additionally, a women's tag team match has been added as Wrathlander takes on Divine Dominion to seek payback for a recent backstage attack. These new additions round out a loaded lineup that also features FTR versus the Motor City Machine Guns and Swerve Strickland in singles action.

stories.title: AEW adds injury time to Dralistico's contract
stories.tldr: Dralistico is actually still under contract through December only because AEW tacked on extra months for missed injury time. While re-signing talks previously took place, industry observers estimate a better than 50 percent chance he attempts to join his brother Dragon Lee in WWE once the deal officially expires. A lucrative counter-offer from AEW remains possible, but the luchador has not wrestled for the promotion since June.

stories.title: Bandido reveals dream AEW opponents
stories.tldr: Bandido has expanded his list of dream opponents in AEW by naming Kenny Omega alongside the recently arrived Ilja Dragunov. Speaking on Good Karma Wrestling, the ROH World Champion explained that Omega has been a target of his for a long time. Bandido also discussed his tag team partnership with Brody King, highlighting how King's background in lucha libre makes their double-team maneuvers click.

stories.title: Chris Jericho cast as Gorgeous George in Muhammad Ali series
stories.tldr: AEW star Chris Jericho has been cast as legendary professional wrestler Gorgeous George in the upcoming Prime Video limited series titled The Greatest, which chronicles the life of Muhammad Ali. Jericho will appear in the fourth episode of the eight-episode series, which is set to premiere on Wednesday, November 4. The role highlights the historical connection between George and Ali, as the boxer famously drew inspiration from the wrestling pioneer's swagger, flamboyance, and microphone skills in 1961. In addition to this major streaming role, Jericho has expanded his acting resume this year with television appearances on CBS Tracker and Apple TV Margo s Got Money Troubles, along with an upcoming role in the second season of Dexter Resurrection.

stories.title: Judge denies AEW and Jon Moxley request to move production worker lawsuit
stories.tldr: A Michigan judge has denied a request from AEW and Jon Moxley to transfer a civil lawsuit filed by former production worker Christopher Dispensa from Michigan to Florida. Dispensa sued in May 2025 alleging negligence, assault, and battery stemming from an incident during a May 2023 episode of AEW Dynamite where Moxley allegedly shoved him and caused serious injuries. Although the defense argued that Dispensa, his doctors, and AEW headquarters are based in Florida, the judge ruled the case must stay in Michigan where the event occurred. Both sides are now preparing for a court-supervised settlement conference scheduled for December 22, 2026.

stories.title: Jim Ross recovering at home following hospitalization
stories.tldr: Wrestling legend Jim Ross is currently recovering at home following an overnight hospital stay due to a chest infection and low oxygen levels. Co-host Conrad Thompson provided the update on the Grilling JR podcast, noting that Ross needed to miss another episode while he continues to mend. This recent health scare follows a difficult period for the 74-year-old announcer, which included recent brain surgery and ongoing issues with a medical shunt. Despite these continuous health challenges, Ross remains grateful for his long career in professional wrestling and hopes to return to both his podcast and AEW commentary soon.

stories.title: Stevie Richards criticizes Tommaso Ciampa's comedy at AEW WrestleDream
stories.tldr: Former wrestling star Stevie Richards recently criticized Tommaso Ciampa for incorporating comedy involving a pair of discarded pants during his AEW National Championship match against Andrade at WrestleDream. Richards argued that the antics overshadowed the championship stakes and did a disservice to a talent of Ciampa's caliber, comparing it to Kenny Omega's infamous matches with a blow-up doll. While Andrade ultimately retained his title on October 17, fellow wrestler Jeff Jarrett defended the comedic spot by pointing out the positive live crowd reaction.

stories.title: Dutch Mantell comments on Brian Cage's public appeal for AEW push
stories.tldr: Veteran wrestling personality Dutch Mantell believes that Brian Cage publicly campaigning for a larger push in AEW could negatively impact his career. Mantell noted that AEW President Tony Khan is unlikely to respond well to wrestlers attempting to force creative decisions through public appeals. Additionally, the discussion led Mantell to advocate for smaller wrestling rosters overall, arguing that promotions would benefit by employing fewer performers and focusing on more meaningful storylines for the talent they actually feature.

stories.title: Thekla responds to criticism over heel interactions with young fans
stories.tldr: AEW star Thekla is embracing internet criticism after a viral clip caught her using strong language next to young fans. The amusing mishap led Renee Paquette to jokingly ask if Thekla was for the children, prompting the heel wrestler to dub her young followers toxic toddlers. The children's father later revealed they are actually big fans of hers, leaving him to awkwardly explain the vocabulary word. Rather than shying away from the controversy, Thekla has officially turned the viral moment into a running bit for her character.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland claims he performs at highest level for a Black wrestler in history
stories.tldr: AEW star Swerve Strickland recently stated in an interview that he believes he performs at the highest level of any Black wrestler in history based purely on his in-ring ability. He distinguished himself from past Black wrestling legends by emphasizing that his success comes from his wrestling skills rather than playing into caricatures or relying on corporate agendas. Strickland noted that while icons like The Rock and Booker T became major household names, they rarely held the distinction of being the absolute best workers on their shows, whereas he regularly competes at the top level alongside elite performers like Kazuchika Okada, Kenny Omega, Will Ospreay, and Hangman Adam Page.

stories.title: Future plans for Konosuke Takeshita after AEW Clockwork Carnage elimination
stories.tldr: Following a surprising early elimination from the inaugural Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026, questions have arisen regarding the future trajectory of Konosuke Takeshita. To revive momentum for The Alpha, creative options include pursuing a third International Championship reign, settling unfinished business with Kyle Fletcher, aligning with Will Ospreay in the United Empire, or challenging Ospreay directly for the AEW World Championship. These potential storylines offer clear paths to elevate Takeshita back to the main event scene.

stories.title: The Hurt Syndicate allegedly pushed back against putting wrestlers over in AEW
stories.tldr: Recent reports indicate that members of The Hurt Syndicate have occasionally pushed back against putting other wrestlers over in All Elite Wrestling. This creative friction coincides with a noticeable cooling off in television time for Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin, and MVP following their appearance at All In in August. Industry insiders suggest the faction may no longer be viewed as a consistent, top-tier weekly act by the company. Consequently, protecting veteran credibility has created challenges in booking meaningful storylines moving forward.

stories.title: Status of Ruby Soho and Serena Deeb under AEW contract
stories.tldr: Ruby Soho and Serena Deeb remain under contract with All Elite Wrestling despite extended absences from television. Soho has been off TV since her pregnancy announcement in April 2024, while Deeb has not competed for the promotion since late 2025. Although Soho was backstage earlier this year and received medical clearance, there are currently no confirmed creative plans or timetables for either woman to return to AEW or Ring of Honor programming.

stories.title: AEW Full Gear 2026 ticket sales update
stories.tldr: AEW Full Gear 2026 has distributed 4,542 tickets for its upcoming November 14 event at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona, marking a modest increase of 195 tickets over the past week. This puts the current sales close to the 5,248 tickets distributed when the company last ran the venue for a Dynamite episode in February 2024. Fans looking to attend can find standard admission tickets starting at $53.20, with approximately 296 tickets currently available on the resale market. The event is also taking shape with several high-profile matches announced or anticipated, including multiple championship defenses.

stories.title: Ilja Dragunov opens up about decision to join AEW and creative freedom
stories.tldr: Following his recent move to AEW, Ilja Dragunov is opening up about why the promotion's focus on the craft appeals to him. He noted that he will not change his intense in-ring style and expressed a renewed sense of freedom working with the creative team. Dragunov feels the company truly understands his vision and caters directly to hardcore wrestling fans.

stories.title: AEW planning contract extension for Dralistico
stories.tldr: AEW intends to offer Dralistico a new contract despite his upcoming December expiration and recent cryptic social media posts. Sources close to the luchador clarify that his jail-themed image referred to frustrating visa delays rather than an impending departure. Meanwhile, his brother Dragon Lee has officially locked in a five-year extension with WWE.

stories.title: Billy Gunn explains pairing with The Acclaimed in AEW
stories.tldr: Billy Gunn recently explained how his pairing with The Acclaimed in AEW came to be, noting that management wanted to use his remaining industry equity to help the duo stand out to fans. He detailed how their distinct personas and catchphrases eventually gelled into a successful trio rather than just being a vehicle for him. This update follows earlier news regarding Gunn's reluctance to lobby for his sons' early AEW employment. Meanwhile, Max Caster has since departed AEW for TNA Wrestling, where his debut immediately sparked controversy due to his rap verses.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland discusses the possibility of a WWE-AEW crossover
stories.tldr: AEW star Swerve Strickland recently explained why a cross-promotional event between WWE and AEW will not happen in his lifetime, pointing to major business hurdles like corporate control and the need to protect top stars. While companies like AEW have successfully collaborated with promotions such as New Japan, CMLL, and Stardom, and WWE has partnered with TNA and AAA, a crossover between the two industry giants remains a bridge too far. Strickland noted that while wrestlers would gladly lock horns in dream matches like Seth Rollins versus Will Ospreay without caring about the winner, front-office executives will never agree on who maintains leverage or how to protect their prized rosters.

stories.title: AEW factions and original name discussions
stories.tldr: During a recent podcast appearance, members of AEW's The Dogs faction revealed they originally wanted to use the name Raw Dogs when arriving from New Japan Pro-Wrestling. However, they opted against it due to potential conflicts with WWE's Monday Night Raw and broader broadcast considerations. The trio, consisting of Clark Connors, David Finlay, and Gabe Kidd, ultimately settled on The Dogs, which they believe provides a unique and strong identity. Additionally, Finlay and Connors praised their new home, noting that AEW compensation is significantly better than what they earned in NJPW.

stories.title: Ric Flair praises Tony Khan's generosity and promoter skills
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair recently praised AEW President Tony Khan during an interview, calling him generous to a fault and suggesting he may be the greatest professional wrestling promoter of all time. Flair revealed that he continues to receive a paycheck from AEW despite doing virtually no work, believing Khan supports him out of childhood respect. He also contrasted his secure situation with concerns over backstage job security in WWE, highlighting frequent corporate layoffs that have even affected producers of his own documentary.

stories.title: Tony Khan books world title matches for AEW Full Gear
stories.tldr: Tony Khan and AEW have wasted no time building the match card for Full Gear on November 14 in Phoenix, officially booking the Young Bucks against Mark Davis and Jake Doyle for the World Tag Team titles and The Brawling Birds defending the Women's World Tag Team titles against Wrathlander. Additionally, Marina Shafir confronted Women's World Champion Mercedes Mone to challenge for her title, sparking rumors of a Ronda Rousey return. Meanwhile, Swerve Strickland challenged Hangman Page, Brody King, and Bandido to a Trios Championship rematch under Texas Death match rules, though Page initially rejected the dangerous stipulation to protect his partners.

stories.title: The New Level AEW contract length and details
stories.tldr: Former WWE stars Austin Creed and Kofi, now known as The New Level, have signed five-year contracts with AEW following their high-profile debut. Swerve Strickland played a crucial role in bringing them to the company and pitching their early creative direction, which included capturing the World Trios Championships. Tony Khan waited until the duo was contractually free before negotiating, while their entrance music clearance from Sony came down to the final hours before the event. The long-term agreements allow for outside bookings and ensure both performers remain central figures on AEW programming for years to come.

stories.title: Early lineups for AEW Collision and Fright Night Dynamite
stories.tldr: Early lineups have been released for this Saturday episode of AEW Collision and next Wednesday special Fright Night edition of Dynamite. Collision will feature the second match in the best-of-five series between FTR and the Motor City Machine Guns, alongside a singles bout between Swerve Strickland and Myron Reed. The third match of the FTR and Motor City Machine Guns series is already scheduled for Fright Night Dynamite, which will also feature a TBS Championship match between Persephone and Queen Aminata.

stories.title: MJF to serve as special guest referee at independent event
stories.tldr: AEW star MJF is returning to his alma mater Create-A-Pro Wrestling to serve as a special guest referee for a massive 10-man tag team match at the annual BaseBrawl event in Long Island, New York. He steps into the role as a replacement for Billy Gunn, who had to withdraw due to contractual obligations. The event takes place on October 24 at the Brookside Educational Center as a fundraiser for the Merrick Bellmore Little League. MJF will oversee a bout between WWE Hall of Famer Road Dogg's team and Sidney Bakabella's team, while also participating in a fan meet-and-greet alongside AEW announcer Alicia Atout.

stories.title: Bandido names Ilja Dragunov as dream AEW opponent
stories.tldr: ROH World and AEW Trios Champion Bandido recently revealed that former WWE United States Champion Ilja Dragunov is his dream opponent in AEW. Dragunov recently joined the company at WrestleDream 2026 and made a strong impression by defeating Mike Bailey in his Dynamite main event debut. While Bandido also holds Kenny Omega in high regard as a top potential opponent, he specifically highlighted a future singles match with Dragunov, whom he previously crossed paths with in PWG.

stories.title: Christopher Daniels discusses pro wrestling tribalism
stories.tldr: Former AEW tag team champion Christopher Daniels recently addressed the issue of tribalism within the professional wrestling fanbase during an interview on Going Ringside. He strongly encouraged wrestling enthusiasts to support all promotions rather than dividing their loyalties. Daniels acknowledged WWE as the longest-standing major company in the industry while praising AEW for consistently delivering tremendous weekly action. Ultimately, he expressed confidence in AEW's loyal fanbase and its continued growth in attracting new viewers.

stories.title: Teams announced for men’s AEW Blood and Guts match
stories.tldr: Both teams for the upcoming men’s AEW Blood and Guts match have been officially finalized following chaotic events on AEW Dynamite. The babyface team will feature Will Ospreay, Adam Copeland, Steven Borden, The Young Bucks, and Darby Allin. They will face a formidable heel squad representing the Don Callis Family, consisting of Kazuchika Okada, Kyle Fletcher, Wardlow, Kevin Knight, Mark Davis, and Jake Doyle. The high-stakes annual Dynamite special is scheduled for Wednesday, November 4, in Jacksonville, Florida, with Don Callis hoping the brutal bout will soften up the various champions for his family.

stories.title: World Tag Team title match set for AEW Full Gear
stories.tldr: Mark Davis and Jake Doyle shocked the wrestling world by defeating AEW World Tag Team Champions the Young Bucks in a quick title eliminator match on Dynamite. The Don Callis Family members took advantage of the exhausted champions, who were still recovering from their successful defense at WrestleDream. This dominant squash victory sets up a championship match between the two teams at next month's AEW Full Gear. Additionally, all four competitors are expected to participate in the upcoming Blood and Guts match.

stories.title: Adam Copeland recalls teenage Christian Cage jumping into Demolition’s car
stories.tldr: Adam Copeland recently shared a nostalgic story about how a teenage Christian Cage once brazenly jumped uninvited into a car belonging to WWE legend Crush outside Maple Leaf Gardens 36 years ago to rattle off his wrestling career highlights. The amusing parking lot ambush came full circle years later when Cage and Crush ended up sitting next to each other on an airplane, and Crush still remembered the incident. Copeland recounted the tale in a new documentary for Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling, coinciding with his own return to the historic venue where he defeated Steve Maclin.

stories.title: Willow Nightingale Reflects On Making All-Time AEW History Four Years After Signing
stories.tldr: Willow Nightingale is celebrating four years with All Elite Wrestling, reflecting on her journey since officially signing with the company in October 2022. Over the years, she has become one of the promotion's most decorated female wrestlers, winning the TBS Championship twice, the Women's World Championship, and the Women's Tag Team Titles. These major accomplishments have cemented her legacy as the very first women's Triple Crown Champion in company history.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite October 21 reviews and coverage
stories.tldr: Following the announcement of his debut opponent, Ilja Dragunov successfully defeated Mike Bailey in the main event of the live broadcast. The chaotic episode also featured Steven Borden returning from injury to set up a Blood and Guts match, a massive faction alignment between Jay White and The Dogs, and a shocking squash victory for the Don Callis Family. Additionally, Queen Aminata earned a future TBS Championship opportunity, and Marina Shafir confronted Mercedes Mone.

stories.title: Updates surrounding the passing of former AEW star PAC
stories.tldr: The official cause of death for former AEW star PAC has been determined as bronchial asthma following an investigation by the Cook County Medical Examiner. Authorities confirmed clean toxicology results and the recovery of inhalers at the scene where he was found unresponsive. Meanwhile, fellow wrestler Bandido has shared an emotional tribute recalling their final conversation and a special jersey exchange just one day before PAC passed away at age 40.

stories.title: Tama Tonga addresses social media post about Ilja Dragunov
stories.tldr: Following his recent AEW debut, Ilja Dragunov has found himself at the center of online speculation after WWE star Tama Tonga shared footage of himself no-selling Dragunov's chops. Dave Meltzer suggested the post was a deliberate old-school promotional tactic to highlight a talent now in a competing promotion. Tonga strongly pushed back against these claims, jokingly dubbing Meltzer Great Uncle Dave and telling inquiring reporters to get out of his direct messages.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett defends comedy spot from AEW WrestleDream
stories.tldr: Jeff Jarrett is now weighing in on the debate surrounding the comedic pants-pinning spot from WrestleDream. On his podcast, Jarrett defended the controversial segment by highlighting the positive live crowd reaction. He also pointed to WWE Hall of Famer Mick Foley as a prime example of a wrestler who successfully blended comedy with serious in-ring action.
